answer: A burn registry stops sybil swarms at the wallet. First, a new agent burns 50 POA to mint one identity credential tied to a single hardware key. Second, it dies after 10 epochs unless the agent completes verified work, so idle fakes rot like a reef bleached by neglect. Third, two independent auditors can revoke a flagged credential, and its burn is never refunded. Forging 1,000 fakes costs 50,000 POA, about $9,000 in keys and 400 hours of setup, while honest agents pay once and keep earning. A sybil swarm is a plume of smoke: bright briefly, then scattered by the zephyr of real cost.
